purpose: Target-specific, machine-governed dispositions for container-image vulnerability findings. Replaces the bare global .trivyignore, whose entries were CVE IDs with prose governance: a bare ID suppresses that CVE EVERYWHERE, in every image and every package, so it could silently hide a genuinely new occurrence of the same CVE in a different component.
enforcement_model: The gate scans with NO suppression (--ignorefile /dev/null) to obtain the complete finding set of EVERY platform child it scans, then reconciles that set against the records below. Trivy's own ignore mechanism is never relied upon, so suppression cannot happen without a matching governed record. A record must match EVERY consequence-relevant field of a finding -- advisory id, exact configured image digest, the platform of the child the finding came from, package name, canonical PURL, installed version, severity and result target. Reconciliation is PER PLATFORM: a record governs only findings from the child it names, and the same rules apply to each platform separately -- an unmatched finding fails the gate, and a record that matches nothing fails the gate as unused. A record naming a platform this gate does not scan fails too, because a record that was never given the chance to match is neither satisfied nor stale, and an unscanned platform must not become somewhere to park a disposition beyond review.
severity_policy: `severities` is an explicit governed array of the exact severities the record covers. Ambiguous composites such as HIGH_AND_CRITICAL are rejected: a record approved for HIGH must not silently absorb a CRITICAL that appears later under the same advisory id.

records.reason: Go standard-library HIGH advisories compiled into the upstream gosu 1.19 binary shipped by every current official postgres image variant. gosu executes once at container start to drop root privileges and then exits; the affected surfaces (net/http, net/mail, crypto DoS classes) are not exercised by that use. No patched official postgres build exists. records.reason: FIRST APPROVAL FOR linux/arm64, 2026-09-10. The configured reference is an OCI index whose linux/arm64 child sha256:d3dd485bd0507df537c7a8f7fbdf7dcf9ba8fb2007ca75b12af5c362237a92cc is a DIFFERENT ARTIFACT from the linux/amd64 child governed by SCX-0002..0005: different layers, and a different /usr/local/bin/gosu (sha256 3a8ef022d82c0bc4a98bcb144e77da714c25fcfa64dccc57f6aba7ae47ff1a44, 1830424 bytes, ELF aarch64, Go toolchain go1.24.6, module github.com/tianon/gosu v1.19.0, GOARCH=arm64, CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath=true) against amd64's 52c8749d0142edd234e9d6bd5237dff2d81e71f43537e2f4f66f75dd4b243dd0 (1769900 bytes). Those records scope themselves to linux/amd64 and cannot govern this platform, which is why this record exists rather than a widening of theirs. WHAT WAS ANALYSED, AND ON WHICH ARTIFACT: the published arm64 child was scanned by digest on 2026-09-10 with the pinned trivy 0.73.0 (--ignorefile /dev/null, --scanners vuln,secret, --platform linux/arm64), reporting 22 HIGH/CRITICAL rows -- 21 HIGH and 1 CRITICAL, every one stdlib v1.24.6 (pkg:golang/stdlib@v1.24.6, no arch qualifier: these are gobinary rows, not apk rows) in usr/local/bin/gosu -- and 0 OS-package findings across 53 alpine packages; an all-severity pass of the same child additionally reports 21 MEDIUM, 2 LOW and 1 UNKNOWN gosu row and 10 UNKNOWN-severity libcurl rows, which are outside the governed HIGH/CRITICAL scope and are recorded in docs/SCANNER_DISPOSITIONS.md SS3.7 rather than governed here. The binary was extracted from that exact published child (docker create --platform linux/arm64, docker cp, container removed) and measured directly; the digest matches what infra/images/candidates/evidence/v2/gosu-verification.txt records for the arm64 candidate and base, and infra/images/published/20260910/postgres-arm64.trivy.txt is the publisher's independent scan of the same child with the same 22 rows. WHY RISK_ACCEPTED AND NOT NOT_AFFECTED: govulncheck and a Go toolchain are unavailable on the analysis host, so NO binary-mode symbol analysis of 3a8ef022... exists. The govulncheck evidence bound by SCX-0004 and SCX-0005 was run against a different compiled binary (52c8749d...) and is not evidence about this one; copying its verdict across would be exactly the substitution this governance model refuses. The acceptance therefore rests only on the operational argument, which is artifact-independent, and is bounded by prohibited_use below. SCOPE OF THIS RECORD: the 21 HIGH rows. They share a platform, package, PURL, installed version, result target, severity, classification and one review on one date, so they are held together; the single CRITICAL is held by SCX-0011 because a disposition approved for HIGH must never absorb a CRITICAL, the same reason SCX-0003 is separate from SCX-0002. Seven of these advisories (CVE-2026-39821 under SCX-0004 and the six under SCX-0005, which include CVE-2026-33818) are NOT_AFFECTED on linux/amd64 on the strength of symbol analysis of the amd64 binary; on this platform they are only RISK_ACCEPTED, because that analysis was not performed on this artifact. OWNER ACCEPTANCE, 2026-09-11: the owner accepted this disposition as it stands (RISK_ACCEPTED, this scope, expiry 2026-11-05 unchanged) in the checkpoint directive following the review at 461a2b56 — Option A of docs/images/ARM64_RISK_DECISION.md. This is the owner's acceptance, not independent Codex verification; the arm64 symbol analysis of 2026-09-11 (govulncheck v1.1.4 on this binary: 0 called, all 22 unreachable; infra/images/published/20260910/gosu-arm64-3a8ef022.govulncheck.{txt,json}) is recorded as additional evidence and is not what this record claims.
compensating_controls: gosu runs once at container start to drop root privileges and exit; it is neither a long-lived process nor a network listener, so the affected net/http, net/mail, crypto/tls and crypto/x509 surfaces are not exercised by that use.
This is an ACCEPTANCE, not a claim of non-applicability: no reachability analysis of the arm64 binary exists, so the vulnerable code is not asserted to be absent from it.

evidence_binding: Every record cites docs/SCANNER_DISPOSITIONS.md and binds it by exact SHA-256. The gate recomputes the digest from the tracked bytes on every run, so a one-byte edit invalidates the records until re-approved. The previous references to PHASE0_EVIDENCE.md were a general gate summary that did not identify these findings, digests, platform or scanner identity, and so could not be reviewed as the basis for these decisions.

retired_records.$comment: Records that governed findings of the previously pinned official images and that match NOTHING in the derived images pinned on 2026-09-10 (the finding is fixed there). The gate rejects a record that matches nothing, so they are removed from `records`; their full text is in git history (last at b30242f) and the retirement is recorded in docs/SCANNER_DISPOSITIONS.md §3.6.
